lesson.menu_title: Passive or Active? -- Describing Regulatory Processes and Tax Reform Mechanisms at ALMA

lesson.subtitle: Lesson 6 -- Passive or Active?
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Leonardo Constantino | Lesson 6 -- Describing Regulatory Processes
lesson.grammar_point: passive voice (present simple, past simple and present perfect passive)

listenings.text: Leonardo, this is Claire Ashworth, head of compliance at Northgate Pay. I have just read the bulletin your team sent, and I need something much shorter for my board. They will not read four pages. What I need is three lines. What was changed, what is now required of us, and what is still open. Two things worry me. The first is the beneficial ownership rule, because our onboarding was built for the old regime, and I am told that nothing was announced before the text was published. The second is the withholding rate. Fifteen percent is a lot of cash, and if we can be held liable for a mistake made by a partner bank, my board will want that in writing. One more thing, and please do not take it personally. Do not send me another document full of by whom and by which. Tell me what happens, and tell me who has to act on Monday morning. Thank you.

Something I learned late, and I wish somebody had told me at your stage. In this profession the passive is not decoration. It is a decision. When you write that a penalty was imposed, you are choosing not to name who imposed it, and nine times out of ten that is the right call, because the client does not care and the sentence is cleaner. But the same habit becomes a real problem in the last paragraph of a memo. If your recommendation says that the documents should be reviewed and the exposure has been assessed, nobody in that company knows who is supposed to do anything on Monday morning. So here is the rule I use, and it has never failed me. Describe the regulation in the passive. Describe the action in the active. The rules were changed, the deadline was moved, the penalty was raised. And then, in the last three lines, your team files the return, we prepare the ruling request, you sign by the twentieth.

extra_audio.text: Let me summarize what has been changed this quarter. The reporting framework was enacted in December, and the first stage is already in force. Two new obligations are imposed on financial institutions this year. Nothing has been decided about the old credit, so we wait for the September bulletin.

reading.rtitle: Regulatory Bulletin -- Third Quarter, Financial Institutions Desk
paras: A new reporting framework was enacted in December, and the first stage is already in force. From January, quarterly returns are filed through a single federal portal, and the amount owed is assessed on the date of filing. Under the old regime, each state authority was notified separately. That requirement has been superseded, and the sector was given no transition period. Nothing was announced before the text was published.

Two obligations are imposed on financial institutions for the first time. Beneficial ownership must be disclosed for every account above two hundred thousand reais, and every cross-border payment is scrutinized before it is cleared. Fifteen percent is withheld at source on some of these payments, unless a treaty rate applies. The rule is enforced by the federal tax authority, and only pension funds are exempt from taxation on these flows. An institution that misses a deadline can be held liable for the full amount, and a penalty of up to four hundred thousand reais is imposed on the group, not on the officer who filed.

Two points are still open. The old credit for financial services has not been phased out yet, although the text says it will disappear by 2027. Last month a decision of the lower court was overturned on appeal. That judgment set a precedent, and every similar ruling is now subject to review. Two further decrees are in the pipeline, but nothing has been decided at federal level and no date has been announced. Clients are advised to wait for the September bulletin before anything is restructured.
